title: Robots
subtitle: Browser robots that visit pages, click, fill forms and extract data for you. Run them by hand, on a schedule or from Flow.

list.title: Your robots
list.emptyHint: A robot opens a browser, follows your steps and hands back the data. Create an empty one or start from a template.
list.name: Name
list.adminOnly: Only workspace admins and owners can create, edit and run robots.

usage.title: This month
usage.perHour: Up to {count} runs per hour · one run at a time per workspace

runner.none: Robots can't run on this server.

runner.sandbox: Runs in an isolated Vercel Sandbox microVM.
runner.local: Runs in a local Chromium on this server.

runner.title: Where it runs

templates.title: Templates
templates.subtitle: Ready-made robots for common sites and tasks. Pick one and adjust it.

scrapeTable.name: Scrape a table to JSON
scrapeTable.desc: Opens a page and turns its first table into rows you can use in Flow.

priceCheck.name: Check a price every day
priceCheck.desc: Reads a product's price daily. Pair it with a Flow on “Robots: run finished” to get alerts.

fillForm.name: Fill a web form
fillForm.desc: Fills fields from inputs, submits and captures the result.

screenshot.name: Take a screenshot of a page
screenshot.desc: Opens a URL, reads the heading and saves a screenshot.

monitorPage.name: Watch a page for changes
monitorPage.desc: Reads a part of a page every hour and emails you the difference when it changes.

listAndDetails.name: List and each detail page
listAndDetails.desc: Extracts a list, then opens every item and reads more fields from its page.

loginExtract.name: Log in and extract
loginExtract.desc: Signs in with a saved credential, skips the login if the session is still open, and extracts a list.

hackerNews.name: Hacker News front page
hackerNews.desc: Stories with rank, title, link and site, two pages, every hour.

githubTrending.name: GitHub trending repositories
githubTrending.desc: Trending repositories with description, stars and stars gained in the period.

githubReleases.name: New releases of a GitHub repository
githubReleases.desc: Checks the releases of a repository daily and emails you when a new one shows up.

lobsters.name: Lobsters front page
lobsters.desc: Stories with tags, score and comments.

devTo.name: DEV posts by tag
devTo.desc: Latest posts of a tag with date and reactions.

remoteJobs.name: Remote jobs from We Work Remotely
remoteJobs.desc: Job posts of a category with company and region, daily, with an email when new ones appear.

booksCatalog.name: Catalog with pages (practice site)
booksCatalog.desc: Books with price and stock across three pages using the Next button.

infiniteScroll.name: Infinite scroll list (practice site)
infiniteScroll.desc: Scrolls down until no new quotes load and extracts them all.

editor.confirmDelete: Delete this robot and its run history?
editor.readOnly: Read only: only admins and owners can edit or run robots.
editor.deleteDesc: Deletes the robot and its whole run history. This cannot be undone.

steps.empty: Pick a type below and add the first one, usually Go to URL.

fields.name: Save as variable
fields.script: JavaScript (body of an async function, return a JSON value)
fields.continueOnItemError: If an item fails, log a warning and go to the next item
fields.paginate: More rows on other pages or further down

steps.templateHint: Use {inputs} for inputs and {vars} for extracted values. Inside a loop: {loopItem}.
tips: Right-click the element → Inspect → Copy → Copy selector, then simplify it.
No good selector? Leave it empty and type the visible text (e.g. “Sign in”). Text is the fallback when the selector finds nothing.
Lists: an Extract with “All matches” over “.item a” returns every link text; add the attribute href to get the URLs.
steps.fileHint: The file is stored and its URL goes to {example}.
steps.credentialsTip: Use {example} with a saved credential. The value never shows up in logs or screenshots.
steps.emptyAltLink: record the steps on the site
steps.cardHint: Matches every card, row or item of the list. Each one becomes a row.
steps.listFieldsHint: Leave the selector empty to read the card itself. Leave the attribute empty to read the text, or use href or src for links and images.
steps.paginateHint: Stops when Next is missing or disabled, when a page repeats or after {max} pages. Each page counts toward the run page limit.
steps.totpTip: Login with a 2FA code: save the secret in a Username and password credential and fill the code field with {example}.
steps.fallbacksHint: Tried in order when the main selector is not on the page. The run log says which one worked.
steps.instructionPlaceholder: Every product with its name, price and link
steps.aiHint: AI reads the page text when the run ends and fills the variable as rows. Later steps of the same run don't see it yet.
steps.scrollHint: Scrolls to the bottom and waits, until no new rows load or after {max} scrolls.
steps.moreHint: Clicks the button until it disappears, no new rows load or after {max} clicks, then reads every row.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.desc: Named values you pass on each run (from the Run dialog, Flow or the schedule's defaults). Use them as {example}.
inputs.empty: Inputs make a robot reusable: a URL, an email or a list that changes on every run.
inputs.name: Name in steps
inputs.label: Label
inputs.passwordWarning: Don't store passwords or secrets here: inputs are saved in plain text and visible to the workspace. Robots are for public pages.
inputs.nameHint: The name used in steps fills in from the label. You can change it.

run.title: Run {name}
run.desc: The robot opens a fresh browser, runs every step and closes it. It can take up to {seconds} seconds.

runs.select: Select a run to see its steps, data and screenshots.
runs.omitted: Too large to keep without Blob storage.
runs.emptyBody: Run the robot to see each step, the data it extracted and the screenshots.
runs.runningHint: The robot is running. Steps and data show up here when it finishes.
runs.queuedNotice: Waiting in line: another robot is running in this workspace. This run starts when it finishes.
runs.warningsNotice: {count, plural, one {# step failed and the robot continued.} other {# steps failed and the robot continued.}} They are marked in the log.

failure.notMatched: The step's selector was not on the page. The snippet shows the page body.
failure.screenshot: The page when the step failed
failure.screenshotAlt: Screenshot of the page when step {step} failed
failure.domPage: HTML of the page (scripts and styles removed)
failure.fixApplied: Step {step} updated. Save to keep it.
failure.fixNone: No better selector found on the captured page.

runs.promoted: Step {step} updated. Save to keep it.
runs.dataset: Table: {added} new · {changed} changed · {removed} not in this run · {total} total
runs.emailSent: Change email sent to {count, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}.
runs.dataHidden: This run used a saved login. Only the person who built the robot and admins can see its data.
runs.autoRefresh: Updating while runs wait in the queue.

settings.enabledHint: When off, the schedule and Flow can't run this robot. You can still run it by hand.
settings.timeoutHint: Max {max} s. Runs count toward your monthly minutes.
settings.flowHint: Add the “Robots: run robot” node and pick this robot. Flows can also react to “Robots: run finished” and “Robots: run failed”.
settings.apiHint: Also from the API v1 (robots:run scope): run it with POST /api/v1/robots/:id/runs or over many inputs with /bulk. Flows can react to “Robots: data changed” when the extracted data differs from the previous run.
settings.responsible: Use robots responsibly: respect each site's terms and robots.txt and don't overload servers. Keep logins in saved credentials, never in steps. Private networks and file:// URLs are blocked; downloads only through the Download step (10 MB max).
settings.cronHint: 5 fields: minute hour day month weekday. E.g. 0 9 * * 1-5
settings.granularity: In the cloud, schedules are checked every 5 minutes: a run can start up to 5 minutes after its time.
settings.sessionHint: Keeps cookies and localStorage (encrypted) so the robot stays logged in.
settings.scheduleDesc: Pick a schedule. For anything finer, use Custom.

presets.noneHint: Runs when you run it or from Flow.
presets.dailyHint: Once a day, at the time you pick.
presets.weekdaysHint: Monday to Friday, at the time you pick.
presets.weeklyHint: Once a week, at the time you pick.
presets.customHint: Every N minutes or hours, or a cron expression.
presets.noneHintOff: Runs only when you run it.

settings.scheduleOff: Automatic runs are off: the schedule will not run until you turn them on.
settings.credentialsDesc: Logins are stored encrypted in Credentials, which Robots shares with Flow. Steps use them without the value showing up in logs or screenshots.
settings.alertsHint: For scheduled and Flow runs. Manual runs never send emails or count as failures.
settings.alerts: Email me when an automatic run fails
settings.pauseCount: {count, plural, one {# failed run} other {# failed runs in a row}}
settings.pauseHint: A paused robot stops scheduled and Flow runs until you turn automatic runs back on. You always get an email when that happens.
settings.retentionHint: Older runs are deleted, along with their screenshots and files.
settings.pausedByFailures: Automatic runs were paused on {date} after several failed runs in a row. Check the Runs tab, then turn them back on.

paste.title: Paste recorded steps
paste.desc: Paste the JSON you copied from the recorder panel.
paste.passwordNote: Passwords arrive as {placeholder}: change LOGIN to the name of a saved credential.
paste.imported: {count, plural, one {# step imported} other {# steps imported}}. Save to keep them.

errors.no_steps: No steps in the pasted text.

paste.modeLabel: What to do with the steps

recorder.title: Step recorder
recorder.subtitle: Do the task once on the site and copy the steps into your robot.
recorder.step1: Drag the button to your bookmarks bar.
recorder.step2: Open the site you want to automate and click the bookmark.
recorder.step3: Do the task: clicks, fields, selects and Enter are recorded. To extract data, use Capture text or Capture list in the panel. If the page changes, click the bookmark again to keep going.
recorder.step4: Click Copy steps in the panel, then use Paste recorded steps in your robot.
recorder.dragHint: Drag it to the bookmarks bar (don’t click it here).
recorder.copyCodeHint: Can’t drag? Paste the code into the browser console on the site.
recorder.selectors: The first stable one wins: data-testid, id, name, aria-label, placeholder, visible text (clicks) and finally a short CSS path. Up to 4 other ones are saved as alternatives, which the robot tries if the page changes.
recorder.passwords: Passwords are never recorded: they become {placeholder} so you can use a saved credential.

panel.hint: Do the task as usual. When done, copy the steps.
panel.pickText: Click the text to extract. Esc cancels.
panel.pickList: Click an item of the list, then the parts of it you want as columns. Click Done when finished.
panel.pickNext: Click the Next or Load more button.

recorder.extractBody: Capture text saves one value. Capture list marks an item that repeats (a product, a row, a result): every similar item becomes a row and each part you click inside it becomes a column. Next page marks the button that loads more rows.

alertEmail.failedBody: The robot "{robot}" failed on a {trigger} run. Error: {error}
alertEmail.throttle: You get at most one failure email per robot every {hours} hours. You can turn these emails off in the robot's Advanced tab.
alertEmail.pausedBody: The robot "{robot}" failed {count} runs in a row, so its automatic runs are paused.
alertEmail.pausedHow: Check the failed run, fix the steps and turn automatic runs back on in the Schedule tab.

builder.desc: Paste a page and say what you want from it. The robot opens the page, finds the list and proposes the columns.

builder.found: {count, plural, one {# column} other {# columns}} · first rows of the page

builder.aiOff: AI is off for this workspace, so these columns were found on the page without AI.
builder.noSample: The columns come from the page HTML. Run the robot to see the rows.

nl.title: Write steps with AI
nl.desc: Describe the task in your own words. AI turns it into steps you can review before adding them.
nl.label: What should the robot do?
nl.placeholder: Go to https://… search for {example}, open the first result and extract the title and the price
nl.urlHint: With a page, AI picks selectors that exist on it.
nl.preview: {count, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}} ready to add
nl.empty: AI could not turn that into steps. Name the page and what to click or extract.
nl.added: {count, plural, one {# step added} other {# steps added}}. Save to keep them.

nl.reviewConfirm: I checked the steps that use a saved login

bulk.title: Run with many inputs

bulk.mapHint: Empty uses the input's default value.
bulk.rows: {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} found
bulk.tooMany: Only the first {max} rows are used.
bulk.start: Queue {count, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}}
bulk.queued: {count, plural, one {# run queued} other {# runs queued}}. They run one after another.
bulk.noInputs: This robot has no inputs. Add inputs first to run it over a list.
bulk.parseError: Could not read the CSV: the first row must have the column names.

data.title: Data across runs
data.desc: Each successful run adds its rows here: new rows, rows that changed and rows that are no longer on the page.
data.enabled: Keep a table of rows across runs
data.noLists: Add an Extract list, Extract table or Extract with AI step to keep a table.
data.keyHint: Columns that identify a row, like the link. With none, the whole row is the key.
data.empty: No rows yet. Run the robot to fill the table.
data.clearDesc: Deletes every row kept across runs. The runs and their data stay.
data.hidden: {count, plural, one {# row was captured} other {# rows were captured}} with a saved login and only show to the robot's builder and admins.
data.aiDesc: A column AI fills for each row, like a category or a yes or no. Up to {rows} rows per run; rows that did not change keep their value.
data.aiPromptPlaceholder: Category of the product, in one word
data.unsaved: Save the robot to apply these settings to the next run.

integrations.changeDesc: An email with the new rows, the rows that left and the values that changed, each time a run differs from the previous one.
integrations.changeToHint: Only people in the workspace. Emails separated by commas. Empty: the person who built the robot. Up to {max} emails a day per robot.
integrations.destDesc: After each successful run, the new and changed rows go to these destinations.

kindHints.crm: Creates or updates contacts by email, or companies by domain.
kindHints.sheets: Keeps a sheet equal to the table, or appends the new rows.
kindHints.airtable: Creates or updates records in a table.

integrations.mappingHint: Pick the column for each CRM field. Contacts need an email; companies need a name or a domain.
integrations.credentialHint: Name of a saved credential: Google (service account or token) for Sheets, a personal access token for Airtable.
integrations.spreadsheetHint: The long id in the sheet URL, between /d/ and /edit. Share the sheet with the service account.

modes.sync: Sync: the sheet matches the table

integrations.baseHint: Starts with app, from the API page of the base.
integrations.mergeHint: With a key field, existing records update instead of duplicating.
integrations.loginWarning: This robot signs in with a saved login, so the rows it sends can include private data. Only send them where that is allowed.
integrations.droppedRecipients: Saved. These addresses are not people in the workspace and were removed from the change email: {list}

geo.title: Country
geo.desc: Pages open with the language and time zone of this country.
geo.label: Country of the runs
geo.proxy: Traffic goes through a proxy in that country, with a new IP on each run.
geo.noProxy: The IP is the server's, so sites that change by IP still see the server's country. A proxy provider set up on the server gives IPs of the country.

export.title: Export
export.desc: Download the robot as a .json file to import it in another workspace. Credentials, saved sessions and runs are not included.
